## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

- **October’s headline revenue is distorted by billing timing and a duplicate.** After removing the duplicate soylent invoice, October cash-billed revenue is **€873.4k** vs September **€797.1k**, up **9.6%**. But **€110k** of the increase is the extra portion of gringotts’ **€120k annual invoice** recognized in October, while professional services fell from **€51.0k to €5.7k**. Underlying monthly recurring revenue per plans is **€757.7k** in October vs **€746.1k** in September, up only **1.6%**.
- **Current run-rate is lower than October’s plan MRR because of churn.** Five customers churned in October, representing **€303.6k ARR / €25.3k MRR**. New October logos add **€133.2k ARR / €11.1k MRR**, plus hooli expanded and soylent contracted. Current active ARR is **€8.789M**, or **€732.4k MRR**, down **1.8% vs September MRR**. So the headline growth is not yet current momentum.
- **SMB is the weakest segment economically and by retention.** SMB is only **€478.8k active ARR / 5.4%** of active ARR, but it had **4 of 5 October churns** and **26.3% gross ARR churn** in October. New SMB logos replaced the lost ARR, but at a lower average ACV. This supports reducing broad SMB/Starter acquisition investment, not necessarily cutting all SMB support.
- **Plan economics favor Pro by margin, but Enterprise remains the profit pool.** In October, Enterprise was **79% of total plan gross profit** but its gross margin fell to **29.5%** as support/infrastructure costs rose. Pro had the best margin at **62.7%**. Starter had the weakest economics at **32.2% margin**, low utilization, and high churn.
- **Acquisition spend should not be increased based on this pack.** The data has funnel lead-to-trial rates and attributed bookings, but **no channel spend, sales cost, retention, or reliable trial-to-paid data**. CAC payback by channel cannot be calculated. Partner/content show higher trial conversion, but samples are small; paid_search is inflated by expansion bookings and has a low trial rate.
- **Recommended posture:** reduce broad SMB/Starter acquisition investment, protect Enterprise reliability and margin, run a focused Pro rate-limit/packaging track, and do not scale any acquisition channel until spend and CAC data are added.

---

## 2. REVENUE & CUSTOMER HEALTH

### Revenue reconciliation

| Item | September | October |
|---|---:|---:|
| Recurring plan MRR | €746.1k | €757.7k |
| Professional services | €51.0k | €5.7k |
| Gringotts annual invoice | n/a | €120.0k |
| Duplicate soylent invoice | n/a | €19.5k excluded |
| Cash-billed revenue in revenue.csv | €797.1k | €873.4k after excluding duplicate |
| Cash-billed revenue if duplicate included | — | €892.9k |

October’s cash increase vs September is **€76.3k**, but the bridge is:

- Recurring plan MRR increase: **+€11.6k**
- Extra annual prepayment vs monthly equivalent: **+€110.0k**
- Professional services decline: **−€45.3k**

So the headline October increase is mostly billing timing, not broad recurring acceleration. Also, October plan MRR of **€757.7k** includes customers who churned during October. Current active MRR is **€732.4k**.

### Current active customer base

| Segment | Active customers | Active ARR | Active MRR | October churn ARR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | 8 | €6,780.0k | €565.0k | €0 |
| Mid-market | 9 | €1,530.0k | €127.5k | €180.0k |
| SMB | 14 | €478.8k | €39.9k | €123.6k |
| **Total** | **31** | **€8,788.8k** | **€732.4k** | **€303.6k** |

October gross churn:

- Mid-market: nakatomi churned at **€180k ARR**; roughly **10.6%** of beginning mid-market ARR.
- SMB: slate, mega-lo-mart, dinoco, and buy-n-large churned for **€123.6k ARR**; roughly **26.3%** of beginning SMB ARR.
- Enterprise: no churn.

New October logos added **€133.2k ARR**, all SMB. So SMB net ARR was slightly positive after new logos, but retention quality is poor: churned SMB average ACV was **€30.9k**, while new SMB average ACV was **€26.6k**.

### Customer health signals

- **Acme:** requests fell from **4.20M to 2.31M**, down **45%**, but tokens fell only **12%** and active users fell only **3%**. The operational note says Acme moved interactive workloads to scheduled batch runs, with an expected 40–50% interactive request reduction. This is therefore not evidence of customer loss or broad demand collapse. Total usage still grew **1.5%** month over month, and excluding Acme it grew about **8.8%**.
- **Soylent:** request volume fell **27%**, revenue fell from **€22.0k to €19.5k monthly**, and support tickets spiked to **8 in October**, including a critical API-errors ticket and several high-severity tickets. This is a real customer-health risk, not just a reporting artifact.
- **Nakatomi:** churned October 19 with **€180k ARR**. It had declining usage and open high-severity support issues before churn.
- **SMB churns:** all four churned SMB customers had large October usage declines around **−35% to −37%**, suggesting deteriorating engagement before churn.

## 3. ACQUISITION

### Funnel lead-to-paid-trial rates

| Channel | Sep leads | Sep paid trials | Sep rate | Oct leads | Oct paid trials | Oct rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Paid search | 520 | 44 | 8.5% | 900 | 58 | 6.4% |
| Content | 260 | 31 | 11.9% | 330 | 34 | 10.3% |
| Partner | 60 | 15 | 25.0% | 75 | 17 | 22.7% |
| Outbound | 160 | 10 | 6.3% | 195 | 11 | 5.6% |

Partner has the highest lead-to-trial conversion, but on a small lead base. Content is second and relatively stable. Paid search has high volume but lower conversion, and it fell from 8.5% to 6.4%.

### Attributed bookings: new logo vs expansion

| Channel | Sep new-logo ARR | Sep expansion ARR | Oct new-logo ARR | Oct expansion ARR | Total new-logo ARR Sep+Oct |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Partner | €166.8k | €0 | €0 | €0 | €166.8k |
| Content | €45.6k | €0 | €45.6k | €18.0k | €91.2k |
| Paid search | €0 | €36.0k | €64.8k | €174.0k | €64.8k |
| Outbound | €33.6k | €0 | €22.8k | €24.0k | €56.4k |

Key points:

- Paid_search’s October attributed revenue is heavily expansion-driven: **€174k expansion** vs **€64.8k new-logo ARR**.
- Partner produced high-value new logos in September but none in October in this pack.
- Content produced steady new-logo ARR across both months.
- Outbound has low lead-to-trial rates.

**CAC payback by channel cannot be calculated.** The pack has no marketing spend, sales cost, gross margin by channel, retention by channel, or trial-to-paid conversion. Funnel “conversions” are paid trials in the same month, not closed paid customers. Acquisition rows mix new logos and expansions.

**Decision supported:** do **not** increase spend on any channel based on this pack alone. If a controlled test is required, partner/content are the more defensible tests because they show higher or steadier lead-to-trial conversion, but partner’s sample is small. Paid search should not be scaled for new-logo acquisition until spend, CAC, and expansion-vs-new-logo attribution are separated.

## 4. PLAN ECONOMICS

October plan economics, €k:

| Plan | Customers | Revenue | Infra cost | Support cost | Gross profit | Gross margin | Sep margin | Utilization: avg requests / included |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Enterprise | 14 | 659.5 | 296.8 | 168.0 | 194.7 | 29.5% | 32.2% | 1.888M / 3.0M = 63% |
| Pro | 9 | 66.2 | 16.1 | 8.6 | 41.5 | 62.7% | 67.5% | 0.442M / 0.6M = 74% |
| Starter | 13 | 32.0 | 11.4 | 10.3 | 10.3 | 32.2% | 34.9% | 0.084M / 0.2M = 42% |

Observations:

- **Enterprise is the profit engine:** **€194.7k gross profit**, about **79% of total plan gross profit**. But margin fell from **32.2% to 29.5%** as support and infra costs grew faster than revenue.
- **Pro has the best unit economics:** **62.7% gross margin**, highest utilization at **74%** of included requests, and revenue grew from **€63.0k to €66.2k**. However support cost rose **24.6%** month over month and rate-limit tickets rose from about **5 in September to 13 in October**, all in Pro. This looks like a packaging/rate-limit product issue.
- **Starter is weak:** **32.2% margin**, only **€10.3k gross profit**, low utilization at **42%**, and it contains most of the SMB churn. Support cost rose **41%** month over month. It does not merit scarce engineering focus unless the goal is automation or churn reduction.

**Plan attention conclusion:** Enterprise deserves the largest defensive engineering attention because it is the largest gross-profit pool and its margin is eroding. Pro deserves a focused secondary product track because it has the best margin and highest utilization, with a clear rate-limit issue. Starter should be treated as a low-touch/automation and qualification problem, not the primary engineering priority.

---

## 5. RECOMMENDATIONS

1. **Segment investment: reduce broad SMB/Starter acquisition investment.**
   - SMB has high churn, lower ACV, low Starter utilization, and weaker plan economics.
   - Do not eliminate SMB entirely; instead tighten qualification, enforce minimum ACV/activation criteria, and automate onboarding/support.
   - Protect Enterprise and do not cut Mid-market blindly: mid-market has meaningful ARR, but Soylent needs immediate customer-success/engineering attention.

2. **Acquisition: do not increase channel spend yet.**
   - Add channel-level spend, sales cost, retention, and gross margin data to calculate CAC and payback.
   - Separate new-logo bookings from expansion bookings in attribution.
   - If running a capped test, test partner/content first, but treat partner as high-variance due small sample.
   - Do not scale paid_search for new logos based on attributed revenue that is mostly expansion.

3. **Product plan focus: protect Enterprise, build Pro.**
   - Enterprise: prioritize API reliability, performance, and cost-to-serve to defend the largest profit pool.
   - Pro: fix rate-limit behavior and improve packaging/overage logic; this plan has the best margin and highest capacity utilization.
   - Starter: avoid major engineering investment unless it directly reduces churn or support cost through automation.

4. **Customer health actions.**
   - Assign a save plan for Soylent given the usage decline, revenue contraction, and critical/high-severity tickets.
   - Treat Acme’s request decline as expected batch-migration behavior, not churn risk, but monitor token volume and support quality.
   - Review SMB churn cohort and acquisition source; replacing churned customers with lower-ACV logos is not healthy growth.

5. **Data/reporting fixes.**
   - Deduplicate invoices by transaction ID.
   - Separate annual prepayments from monthly recurring revenue.
   - Report current active ARR/MRR separately from plan MRR that includes mid-month churn.
   - Track trial-to-paid conversion by channel and cohort.

---

## 6. UNCERTAINTIES / DATA ISSUES

- **Duplicate invoice:** `INV-2026-10-0209` appears twice for soylent, once from `stripe` and once from `billing_sync`, each €19.5k. I excluded one; including both would overstate October revenue by **€19.5k**.
- **Annual invoice timing:** gringotts’ **€120k** annual subscription is billed in October but covers 12 months. Only **€10k** is the October monthly equivalent; the remaining **€110k** is prepayment for future periods. Cash-billed revenue and recurring revenue should not be compared directly.
- **Professional services are non-recurring:** September had **€51k** professional services; October had **€5.7k**. This materially affects month-over-month revenue comparisons.
- **Churned customers remain in plan data:** October plan MRR includes nakatomi and the four churned SMB customers. Current active MRR is lower. The churned customers’ `arr_eur` values in the customer file should not be included in current ARR.
- **Acquisition attribution is not CAC:** attributed revenue is marketing-credited ACV at conversion and mixes new logos with expansions. Expansion bookings take effect the following billing cycle. There is no spend data, so CAC, CAC payback, ROI, and channel efficiency cannot be calculated.
- **Funnel conversions are not paid customers:** funnel “conversions” are paid trials in the same month. Trial-to-paid conversion is not tracked in the pack, so channel-to-customer conclusions are unreliable.
- **Support cost is plan-level, not per ticket:** support cost includes fully loaded customer-success staff. Ticket counts and support cost cannot be used to derive precise cost-per-ticket or causal ROI.
- **Usage changes require context:** Acme’s request decline is explained by the batch migration note; tokens fell much less than requests. `usage_change_pct` is missing for new customers, so absolute requests must be used for those accounts.
- **No data on sales capacity, cash collection, contract duration, churn reasons, customer profitability by channel, or competitive dynamics.** Decisions should therefore be framed as supported/not supported by this pack, not as definitive causal conclusions.
